objectives: Compare vaccine platforms + their immunogenicity + durability.
Design + monitor immunization programs (EPI, cold chain, coverage, equity, AEFI).
Reason about major successes (smallpox, polio, measles, HPV, COVID) + remaining gaps.

slides.title: Vaccine platforms, immunogenicity, + durability
slides.body:
**Vaccines** induce protective adaptive immunity by presenting antigens in a controlled, non-pathogenic context. Detailed mechanism (germinal centers, affinity maturation, memory B + T cells, plasma cells) is covered in P68 (immunologist). Here we focus on platforms, programmatics, + population effects.

**Major vaccine platforms**:
- **Live attenuated** — replication-competent but weakened pathogen. Strong, durable immunity (often lifelong). Examples: measles + mumps + rubella (MMR; Hilleman; Plotkin), varicella, yellow fever 17D (Theiler 1937 — Nobel), oral polio (Sabin), BCG (Calmette + Guérin 1921), rotavirus (Rotarix + RotaTeq), influenza FluMist. Cold-chain sensitive; contraindicated in immunocompromised.
- **Inactivated whole-pathogen** — killed pathogen. Examples: inactivated polio (Salk), hepatitis A, rabies, Japanese encephalitis, Sinovac CoronaVac. Safer but less durable; multiple doses needed.
- **Subunit + recombinant protein** — purified antigen ± adjuvant. Examples: hepatitis B (HBsAg; recombinant DNA — first GE vaccine; Hilleman 1981), HPV (Cervarix Gardasil; VLPs), pertussis acellular, COVID-19 Novavax (NVX-CoV2373 spike + Matrix-M).
- **Conjugate** — polysaccharide linked to carrier protein → T-cell-dependent response. Required for protection in <2 yr olds. Examples: Hib (Robbins + Schneerson + Anderson; Nobel-deserving 1990s), pneumococcal PCV7/13/20, meningococcal ACWY + B.
- **Toxoid** — chemically detoxified bacterial toxin. Examples: diphtheria + tetanus + pertussis (DTP/DTaP).
- **Viral vector** — engineered virus delivers antigen gene. Examples: ChAdOx1 (Oxford-AZ COVID-19), Ad26 (J&J COVID-19; Ebola), rVSV-ZEBOV (Ebola; Henao-Restrepo 2015 ring vaccination Guinea trial).
- **mRNA** — lipid nanoparticle delivers mRNA encoding antigen. Examples: BNT162b2 Pfizer-BioNTech (Sahin + Türeci) + mRNA-1273 Moderna for COVID-19 (Karikó + Weissman; Nobel 2023). Rapid design (weeks from sequence), high immunogenicity, but cold-chain demanding.
- **DNA + self-amplifying RNA + virus-like particles (VLPs)** — emerging.

**Adjuvants** — boost + modulate the immune response:
- **Alum** (aluminum salts; Glenny 1926) — workhorse; Th2-skewed.
- **MF59** (squalene; Flu Q-Pan H5N1).
- **AS01** (MPL + QS-21; RTS,S malaria + shingles).
- **CpG ODN** — TLR9 agonist (Heplisav-B).
- **Matrix-M** (Novavax).
- Newer adjuvants enable strong Th1 + CD8 + mucosal responses.

**Immunogenicity metrics**:
- **Seroconversion rate** — fraction reaching detectable antibody threshold.
- **Geometric mean titer (GMT)** — central tendency of antibody titers.
- **Neutralization titer** — functional virus neutralization (gold standard for many vaccines).
- **Vaccine efficacy (VE)** = 1 - (incidence_vacc/incidence_unvacc). Measured in Phase 3 RCT.
- **Vaccine effectiveness** — real-world performance from observational + test-negative designs.

**Durability + waning**:
- **Tetanus + diphtheria**: boosters every 10 yr.
- **Pertussis** (aP): waning over 3-5 yr; resurgence in adolescents.
- **HPV**: durable >12 yr; possibly lifetime.
- **Yellow fever**: lifetime after 1 dose.
- **Measles (MMR)**: durable lifetime in most.
- **COVID-19 mRNA**: 3-6 mo against infection; ~12+ mo against severe disease.
- **Influenza**: ~6-12 mo, must be redesigned annually.

slides.title: EPI + cold chain + Gavi + vaccine confidence
slides.body:
**Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI)** — launched by WHO 1974 under Henderson + Keja + Yach. Standard EPI portfolio originally: **BCG, DTP, OPV, measles**; later extended with hepatitis B, Hib, pneumococcal, rotavirus, HPV, meningococcal A (Africa), yellow fever. By 2024, immunization saves ~5 million lives annually.

**Routine schedule** (typical LMIC, EPI-aligned):
- Birth: BCG, OPV0, HepB.
- 6, 10, 14 wk: DTP-HepB-Hib (pentavalent), OPV, PCV, rota.
- 9 mo + 15-18 mo: measles + rubella (MR or MMR).
- 9-14 yr (girls + boys): HPV.
- HCWs + travelers + risk groups: additional.

**Cold chain** — vaccine potency depends on temperature integrity from manufacturer to arm. Standard 2-8 °C; some live (varicella) frozen; mRNA -20 to -70 °C. Cold chain components: refrigerators (gas + solar), vaccine carriers, ice packs, freeze indicators (Vaccine Vial Monitors VVM), training, supervision. Last-mile delivery is a recurrent failure point. Cold-chain innovations: Project Optimize, drones (Zipline Rwanda + Ghana), thermostable formulations (vaccine vial monitors, MR thermostable in development).

**Vaccine wastage** — open-vial waste from multidose vials. Multidose vial policy + Universal Mass Vaccination policy balance access vs waste.

**Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance** — founded 2000 (Gates + WHO + UNICEF + World Bank + governments). Pools demand + finances vaccines for the poorest countries. Pneumococcal + rotavirus + HPV scale-up driven by Gavi's Advance Market Commitment (AMC). Gavi co-financed ~half the world's children's vaccinations by 2022. Funded COVAX during COVID-19. Gavi 5.0 strategy (2021-25) + 6.0 (2026-30) emphasize zero-dose children + sustainability.

**Vaccine confidence + the 3 Cs (WHO SAGE)** — convenience, complacency, confidence. Vaccine hesitancy is not new (Jenner 1796 cowpox skeptics; smallpox riots; OPV pulse-polio resistance in Nigeria 2003-04). The **Vaccine Confidence Project** (Heidi Larson, LSHTM 2010+) globally surveys confidence; her book 'Stuck' (2020) documents drivers (post-truth, mistrust of institutions, distrust of pharma, social-media amplification).

**WHO SAGE (Strategic Advisory Group of Experts on Immunization)** — issues evidence-based recommendations on vaccines + schedules. Independent expert body.

**Vaccination strategies**:
- **Routine immunization (RI)** through health system.
- **Supplemental immunization activities (SIAs)** — periodic mass campaigns (measles, polio, MR).
- **Ring vaccination** — vaccinate contacts of cases + their contacts (smallpox; Ebola rVSV-ZEBOV).
- **Catch-up + multi-age campaigns** — close immunity gaps.
- **Targeted high-risk groups** — health workers (HBV), adolescents (HPV), elderly (zoster, influenza, pneumococcal).

**Equity in immunization** — IA2030 (Immunization Agenda 2030, WHO) prioritizes 'zero-dose children' (the ~14 million children annually who receive *no* routine vaccines, concentrated in conflict + remote + urban-poor settings). Equity index: WHO + UNICEF monitor coverage by wealth quintile, urban/rural, sex, region.

slides.title: Coverage, AEFI surveillance, + the major program success stories
slides.body:
**Coverage measurement** — multiple methods, often discordant:
- **Administrative coverage** — doses given / target population. Cheap, real-time, but susceptible to denominator + numerator error (migration; double-counting; eligibility).
- **Surveys** — DHS (Demographic + Health Surveys; ICF + USAID), MICS (UNICEF), WHO Coverage Cluster Surveys. Household-level home-based-record review + maternal recall. Costly + episodic but valid.
- **Serosurveys** — measure population antibody prevalence; ground truth for immunity but expensive + sometimes ambiguous (post-vaccine vs post-infection).
- **Pareto principle (80/20)** — typically 20% of districts contain 80% of unvaccinated children. Drives geographically targeted catch-up.
- **Equity dashboards** — disaggregate by sex, wealth, urban/rural; identify gaps.

**WUENIC** — WHO + UNICEF Estimates of National Immunization Coverage; consensus-based annual estimates, peer-reviewed, published in WHO Vaccine-Preventable Diseases Monitoring System.

**Adverse Events Following Immunization (AEFI) surveillance**:
- **Definition** — any adverse event after vaccination, whether causally linked or not.
- **Reporting systems**: VAERS (US; CDC + FDA passive); V-safe (US; mobile-based active); VSD (Vaccine Safety Datalink, ~14M+ enrollees, active surveillance via 9 integrated US health systems); EudraVigilance (EU); Yellow Card (UK); India national AEFI scheme; Vigibase (WHO global).
- **Brighton Collaboration** — standardized case definitions for AEFIs (anaphylaxis, encephalitis, Guillain-Barré, intussusception, myocarditis). Enables comparability across systems.
- **Signal detection** — disproportionality (PRR, ROR), self-controlled case series (Farrington), background-rate comparison. Strict separation between temporal coincidence + causal association.
- **Risk communication** — narrow window from signal to action; case studies in mistakes (Cutter polio 1955; H1N1 narcolepsy 2009; thiomerosal MMR 1998 Wakefield retraction; Dengvaxia 2017 Philippines; COVID-19 ChAdOx1 thrombosis).

**Major immunization program successes**:

**Smallpox Eradication Programme (SEP)** — WHO 1967-1980, led by D. A. Henderson (US CDC); Frank Fenner (Australian) chaired Global Commission for Certification. Strategy: shift from mass vaccination (impossible to achieve high enough coverage) to **surveillance + containment + ring vaccination** (Foege + Henderson). Bifurcated needles + freeze-dried lyophilized vaccine + heat-stable. Last endemic case Ali Maow Maalin 1977 Somalia; declared eradicated 1980 by 33rd WHA. ROI: $300M campaign saves ~$1B+/yr ever since. Only human disease ever eradicated. Henderson's book 'Smallpox: The Death of a Disease' (2009) is definitive.

**Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI)** — launched 1988 (Rotary + WHO + UNICEF + CDC + Gates Foundation since 2009). Cases reduced from ~350,000 (1988) to <10 wild cases/yr (2020s). WPV2 eradicated 2015; WPV3 2019; WPV1 endemic in Afghanistan + Pakistan only. Mass + supplementary OPV campaigns; switch from tOPV to bOPV 2016 (sync globally to eliminate cVDPV2); novel OPV2 (nOPV2) for cVDPV outbreak response 2020+. Lessons: campaign + RI must coexist; community resistance (Nigeria 2003-04 OPV boycott) costly; surveillance via AFP cases + environmental sewage sampling.

**Measles + rubella (MR) elimination** — Americas region declared measles-free 2016 (briefly lost 2018); WHO 2024 strategy aims for global elimination. Challenges: requires >95% 2-dose coverage; mass migration + conflict create gaps; vaccine hesitancy clusters (Brooklyn 2019, Samoa 2019). MR vaccine durable + cheap; Gavi-supported.

**HPV vaccination — Australia + Rwanda models** — Australia introduced quadrivalent in 2007 + 9-valent 2018; school-based program with ~80% coverage. Brotherton + Garland documented >90% decline in vaccine-type HPV in young women within a decade. Cervical cancer elimination feasible (Hall + Brisson 2019). Rwanda + Bhutan achieved high coverage in LMIC settings via school-based campaigns. WHO 90-70-90 strategy.

**COVID-19 vaccination + COVAX** — 13 EUA vaccines deployed within 12 months; >13 billion doses by 2024. **COVAX** (Gavi + CEPI + WHO) aimed at equitable allocation; fell short of equity goals (LMIC delayed vs HIC) — major lesson for future pandemic preparedness. Operation Warp Speed (US 2020), EUAs, mRNA + viral-vector vaccines as platform technologies. Modeling: Watson + Ghani 2022 Lancet ID estimated >14 million deaths averted in the first year of COVID-19 vaccines.

question.question: Designing a measles catch-up campaign in a district with low coverage
question.goal: A district of 200,000 children under 5 has DPT3 coverage 70% + MR1 coverage 55%. There is a measles outbreak in a neighboring district. Plan a catch-up SIA + estimate impact.

steps.prompt: What is the HIT for measles + what coverage does your district currently meet?
steps.reveal: Measles HIT = 1 - 1/16 ≈ 93.75%. With MR vaccine effectiveness ~97%, target coverage = 93.75/0.97 ≈ 97%. District MR1 of 55% is far below; measles spread is virtually certain on importation.

steps.prompt: What target population for the SIA?

acceptedAnswers: all children 9 mo - 5 yr or wider; ~200,000 + adolescents

steps.reveal: Target all children 9 mo - 5 yr (200k), preferably extended to <15 yr to close cohort gaps. Wide-age-range SIAs are standard when accumulated unvaccinated cohorts pose risk. Coverage target: 95%+ in the SIA. Combine MR or MMR depending on schedule.

Doses = target × 1/(1 - wastage). At 10% wastage: 200,000 / 0.9 ≈ 222,000 doses. Plan syringe + safety box supply, cold-chain capacity, transport, supervision teams, AEFI hotline. Pre-position vaccines + microplan by sub-district + dispatch mobile teams to hard-to-reach + nomadic populations.

steps.prompt: How would you monitor coverage in real time + verify post-campaign?

acceptedAnswers: admin tally + LQAS (lot quality assurance) + post-campaign coverage survey + serosurvey

steps.reveal: (a) Daily admin tally vs target; (b) LQAS by sub-district (Lemeshow) to flag low-coverage clusters during the campaign; (c) post-campaign coverage survey (cluster sampling, 30×7 or 30×10) within 4 wk; (d) serosurvey ~6 mo post-campaign to validate. Triangulation avoids over-reliance on admin numbers, which often overestimate. Equity disaggregation by wealth, urban/rural, sex.

acceptedAnswers: passive + active surveillance + Brighton case definitions + rapid response team + risk communication plan

steps.reveal: Pre-train clinicians + AEFI focal persons; activate passive surveillance + monitor sentinel sites for serious AEFIs (Brighton definitions for anaphylaxis, encephalitis, seizures); establish national + state AEFI causality-assessment committee; baseline event rates to interpret signals (e.g., febrile seizures ~5/10,000 doses MMR is expected, not concerning); prepare media briefings + spokesperson; partner with community + religious leaders; pre-rehearse vaccine-misinformation responses (Vaccine Confidence Project playbooks).

question.question: Why is the ring-vaccination strategy historically associated with smallpox eradication + the 2014-16 Ebola Guinea trial (rVSV-ZEBOV)?
options: Ring vaccination identifies cases + vaccinates their contacts + contacts-of-contacts. Highly effective when: (a) the disease has a clear case-to-contact transmission chain; (b) vaccine acts fast enough (within incubation period) to prevent secondary cases; (c) routine mass vaccination coverage is infeasible (smallpox campaign was already underway; rVSV-ZEBOV was investigational). Henderson + Foege showed it could eradicate smallpox by interrupting transmission with much less vaccine than mass campaigns. The Henao-Restrepo 2015 Guinea rVSV-ZEBOV trial used a cluster-randomized ring design + showed >97% efficacy.
question.explanation: Ring vaccination targets the transmission chain rather than the whole population. Henderson + Foege + the SEP (1967-1980) shifted smallpox strategy from mass vaccination (impossible to achieve ~85% HIT in many settings) to surveillance + containment + ring vaccination — a much more efficient use of vaccine + identified active transmission corridors. The Ebola Guinea ring-vaccination trial (Henao-Restrepo + Henao-Restrepo et al. 2015 Lancet; followed up 2017) used a cluster-randomized stepped-wedge ring design to evaluate rVSV-ZEBOV (Merck) during an active outbreak; showed >97% protective efficacy. Logic: vaccine acts fast (rVSV-ZEBOV in days), disease has clear contact chains, mass vaccination infeasible during emergency. Generalizes to other emergency-use vaccines (Mpox 2022).

hints: Used when mass coverage is infeasible.
slides.workedSolution: Ring vaccination targets contacts of cases + their contacts. Used for smallpox eradication (Henderson + Foege) + Ebola Guinea trial (Henao-Restrepo 2015 rVSV-ZEBOV >97% efficacy). Logic: case-to-contact chains + rapid-acting vaccine + infeasibility of mass campaigns.

question.question: Introducing HPV vaccine in a LMIC: school-based vs facility-based delivery
question.prompt: A LMIC Ministry of Health plans to introduce 1-dose HPV vaccine (WHO SAGE 2022 reduced from 2 doses for 9-14 yr) for girls aged 9-14 (~1.5 million eligible/yr). Discuss: (a) school-based vs facility-based delivery (coverage, equity, out-of-school girls, boys); (b) Gavi co-financing + cold-chain implications; (c) AEFI preparedness + Brighton case definitions; (d) communication strategy + vaccine confidence (Heidi Larson framework — anticipating cancer-prevention messaging, sexual-debut concerns, religious + cultural sensitivities); (e) coverage measurement (school records + DHS + admin); (f) integration with school health + adolescent reproductive health; (g) bridge to 90-70-90 cervical-cancer elimination targets; (h) what specific lessons from Australia (Brotherton + Garland) + Rwanda + Bhutan would you incorporate.

question.question: Measles vaccine effectiveness against infection is 97% per dose. To achieve a 95% immune population requires what 2-dose MMR coverage? Round to nearest percent.
question.hint: Required coverage × 0.97 ≥ 0.95 (assuming 1 dose for simplicity). Coverage ≥ 0.95/0.97 ≈ 0.979 ≈ 98%.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why vaccine *confidence* + AEFI surveillance are as important to a successful immunization program as biological efficacy + cold chain — using a contemporary example.
question.rubric: Mentions: high vaccine efficacy is necessary but not sufficient; programs need (a) cold-chain integrity (potency); (b) AEFI surveillance (VAERS, VSD, Brighton Collaboration) to detect rare safety signals + assess causality (Cutter polio 1955, MMR + Wakefield 1998 retracted, COVID-19 ChAdOx1 + VITT); (c) vaccine confidence (3Cs: confidence, complacency, convenience; Heidi Larson Vaccine Confidence Project) — confidence collapses can drop coverage rapidly (Philippines Dengvaxia 2017 → 30% drop in routine immunization). Example: COVID-19 — high vaccine efficacy + cold chain met fragmented confidence; differential uptake across countries + sub-populations widened inequities + extended pandemic. Conclude: a vaccine that nobody takes has 0% effectiveness; confidence + surveillance are co-equal pillars.
